correctness.rationale: The exact Laplacian four-eigenspace decomposition yields five covariance entries, and all pair orbits reduce to three 2x2 rational scores. Two exact quartic identities were independently checked symbolically; the normalized q to the negative third power quartics tend to p-2-2t-t² and t²-p, each with a simple positive root for p at least three. For sufficiently large q the coefficient sign patterns force unique positive roots by Descartes and the limiting order separates them. Their signs give the complete optimum orbit classification and ties. A 7,082-assertion exact verification checks all pair scores against direct inverses on independently generated rational matrices. No finite enumeration is used to prove the infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: The accessible primary literature establishes general Gaussian covariance placement and Nyström trace loss, but not the specified three strict optimal pair phases with the two universal radical limiting thresholds for every fixed p at least three. A related two-vertex smaller-part case calculation is not covering: that first transition is degenerate and cannot imply a positive first threshold at p at least three. Searches and precise comparisons were conducted; inaccessible contemporary material remains a qualified publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: Two-landmark Nyström posterior-trace minimization is a natural covariance design objective, with exactly three selection orbits on K_{p,q}. A universal positive threshold for the first same-shore to mixed-shore transition and a second threshold at square root of p describe a qualitative change over the previously understood two-vertex smaller-part case boundary. Exact formulas, ties, a proof for every fixed p at least three at large q, and constructive finite-pair coefficient tests make the result a motivated analytic design classification rather than an arbitrary numerical example.
